newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol sees net earnings doubling by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Repsol sees net earnings doubling by 2001.

text.p: Spanish energy group Repsol expects its net and operating profits to double by 2001, chairman Alfonso Cortina said on Wednesday.

"By the year 2001, Repsol will be a bigger and more profitable company. Total assets will have increased 30 percent. We think we can achieve earnings on capital employed of around 15 percent and a return on equity of around 20 percent," he said.
"Both operating profit and net profit will have doubled (by the year 2001)," Cortina added at a presentation of the share offer to analysts.
In the last leg of Repsol's privatisation, the government is selling its remaining 10.0 percent stake.
Cortina said Repsol plans to invest 370 billion pesetas in Latin America in the next five years.
"Our target for Latin American expansion is to position ourselves as the leading integrated energy company in that area," he said.
Repsol posted net 1996 profit of 119.22 billion pesetas.
